chapter: Buddy Petit and brass band reading
title: Downtown reading bands versus uptown faking in brass bands
summary: Ridgley says the Excelsior and Onward bands downtown had reading musicians while most faking came from uptown, and recalls the musicians he met working at a country grocery as a boy.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Reading music versus faking and playing by ear

blocks.x: When did they start playing by head in the street, in parades and funerals?

Well, the, you see, the Excelsior band and the Onward band, those bands from downtown, the old man George Moret was at Excelsior, and Manuel Perez was the Onward band. Well, those fellows always had, uh, reading musicians, see, they had better reading musicians downtown than they did uptown, see? They were real better musicians, plenty of them. And the most of the faking was from uptown, I guess. But that had been going on with them up there a long time. See, they go to Manmoretti and them and they ain't bad man. They knew if you did not read you couldn't play with them.
They had to play your voice.

And Manmoretti would be a whole lot like that, too. They always had all good reading men. But they were all good musicians from downtown, those Creole people. I knew them all because I worked in the country grocery in Jefferson, Paris. And it was about a mile and a quarter out of the city limit. And they used to hire those fellows. They played fumes and all like that and parades and everything. Well, I knew all those old musicians' names from Wike and that Stewart. I had to stop there to get where they was going, see. I'd know them. I used to take them in and give them a big cool drink of water and some of them. I'd give them a drink of whiskey. I had the privilege I could do that. And they all got to know me. I'd know them all of them once by then. People used to wonder how I know them all of them. That's from when I was in the country before I came to New Orleans. And I worked in the country grocery from about 11 years old until I got married and see, I'd wait for them for about 18 years. And then the people helped me along with my music business and helped me with everything. It was very good to me. I still even hit one of them.
But did they have any brass bands that just played by head uptown when you were a little boy?

No, no. They all were spelled. They had to read them. They had to read them. Somebody had to read to play them. Most of them. You couldn't handle no brass bands. They didn't. They weren't trying to play some marches and punes and things like that. They had to read, but some of them could fake. They were pretty good.
When did they start playing? They were playing fake numbers in the street like they do now.
I already knew them to do it.
They would always play some fake numbers.
They always did know them to do it.
